 This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Made The Following:
 Order

1. Accused no.1 in Crime No.281/2023 registered by Belur Police Station, Hassan District, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 34 IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, is before this Court under Section 438 Cr.PC.
2.
Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.

3. On the complaint of Anupallavi.H.P. who is the wife of the petitioner herein, FIR in Crime No.281/2023 was registered by Belur police against the petitioner and eight others for the aforesaid offences.
Apprehending arrest in the said case, petitioner had filed Crl. Misc. No.1316/2023 before the Court of II Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Hassan, which was rejected on 10.11.2023.

entities.text: II Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, he is before this Court.
4. Learned Counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition, has prayed to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.
From a reading of the complaint averments, it is seen that the complainant's wife who is the complainant in the present case undisputedly is staying in her parents house from 22.04.2023 onwards.

7. In the complaint, it is averred that on 21.05.2023, the complainant has given birth to a boy child and on 22.05.2023, petitioner and his relatives had come to the hospital and after seeing the child they had returned and thereafter, they had not contacted the complainant.

It is further averred that on 05.10.2023 she had called her husband and had informed that she would come to Bengaluru, but Sri. Ramu @ Rama N.R vs State Of Karnataka on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107767312/
2 thereafter the petitioner had called her and informed her not to come to Bengaluru.

entities.text: Sri. Ramu @ Rama N.R vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The allegation in the complaint is that the accused persons have ill- treated the complainant after marriage.
8. Omnibus allegations are made in the complaint.
The alleged offences are triable by the Court of Magistrate and maximum punishment for the said offences is imprisonment by three years.

Considering the fact that for the last six months, the complainant has been staying in her parents house and the complaint is belated lodged on 20.10.2023, I am of the view NC: 2023:KHC:45410 that prima facie the petitioners have made out a case for grant of anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, the following order:
9.
The petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest in Crime No.281/2023 registered by Belur Police Station, Hassan District, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 34 IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961,
subject to the following conditions:

1. The Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
2. Petitioner shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.
3. Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and he shall co-operate with the police for investigation and appear before them whenever called upon.
NC: 2023:KHC:45410 4.
The petitioner shall not involve in similar offences in future.
